desk.headline: Revenue up 55% to a record $2.18bn and EPS $4.30, beat; Q4 revenue outlook of $2.37–2.40bn above estimates
results: Revenue rose 55% to a record $2.18bn and net income 72% to $1.44bn, a 66% net margin.
Diluted EPS was $4.30, up from $2.45 a year ago.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 59% to $1.84bn, lifting the margin to 84% from 82%.
Operating cash flow and free cash flow were each about $1.4bn; $1.4bn was spent repurchasing and withholding 4.1m shares.
The board added $3.2bn to the buyback, taking the total authorisation to $3.6bn at end-October; cash stood at $3.2bn against $3.5bn of long-term debt.

guidance.summary: For Q4 2026 AppLovin expects revenue of $2.365–2.395bn and adjusted EBITDA of $1.995–2.025bn (84–85% margin). The revenue range is above the analyst figure cited in coverage.

points: Revenue beat the top of the company's own guidance by about $100m; gaming revenue grew close to 50% y/y.
Spending by non-gaming (consumer and e-commerce) advertisers grew by double digits from Q2 and triple digits y/y; no split by vertical was given.
A new generation of ad models was only partly rolled out, with management seeing room to improve further, especially for newer and smaller advertisers.
Management said buybacks were stepped up because the share price looked out of line with its view of value.
Cautions: hard-to-forecast model gains, a growing seasonal swing (strong Q4, weaker Q1) from e-commerce, and ongoing compute spending; connected-TV ads still early.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via TradingView, 4 Nov 2026; BigGo Finance, 4 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)
